documents.unit: University of Colorado system (Office of Policy and Efficiency), applies to CU Boulder
documents.title: APS 6012 - Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.summary: A University of Colorado system policy, effective August 2026, covering responsible AI use in academic, research and administrative work. It mainly sets data, IP, procurement, disclosure and governance rules, and states that it "does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework", leaving that to faculty and units.
documents.stance_why: The document says "this policy does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework" and lets schools, colleges, departments or programs set their own guidance, so it takes no coursework stance itself and delegates.

units.why: The brief description says the University is "committed to supporting the responsible exploration of the rapidly growing field of AI tools while encouraging and supporting innovation"; it is a university-wide statement of purpose, so P56 and an encouraging unit stance.
units.anchor: committed to supporting the responsible exploration of the rapidly growing field of AI tools

units.why: "establishes a basic framework for the responsible, ethical, and secure use of AI" states the purpose and scope of the whole policy, which is P56.
units.anchor: establishes a basic framework for the responsible, ethical, and secure use of AI

units.why: The definition "a subset of Artificial Intelligence (AI) that can generate text, images, code, music or other forms of synthetic content" sets what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: can generate text, images, code, music or other forms of synthetic content

units.why: This sentence says faculty responsibility for pedagogy "includes decisions about the use of AI tools"; it assigns the coursework AI decision to faculty rather than setting a rule, so P04. It is faculty collectively (tenured and tenure-track with participation) rather than each instructor, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: includes decisions about the use of AI tools within those contexts
units.fit_note: Responsibility is placed on tenured and tenure-track faculty with other faculty participating, citing Regent Law 5.A.1.B, not on each instructor individually.

units.why: "final decision-making authority on the use of AI at CU rests with the President and the Chancellors" names who holds authority outside academic contexts; P80 (who owns and decides).
units.anchor: final decision-making authority on the use of AI at CU rests with the President and

units.why: "must comply with CU’s data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies" requires any AI tool use for university work to follow existing policies, which is P77.
units.anchor: must comply with CU’s data security, privacy, and intellectual property policies

units.why: Users "need to consider the security, privacy and handling of any information they provide to GenAI tools and vendors"; this is advice to protect data when using tools, P50.
units.anchor: consider the security, privacy and handling of any information they provide to GenAI tools and

units.why: The same sentence adds "evaluating the quality and accuracy of the output of the system"; this is a separate rule that users check output, so P31 (the data point is coded separately under P50).
units.anchor: evaluating the quality and accuracy of the output of the system

units.why: "AI should be used in ways that are consistent with the University’s mission of education, research, service, and public impact" is a principle that frames all AI use, so P56.
units.anchor: AI should be used in ways that preserve academic freedom, safeguard privacy and institutional data

units.why: The policy says to "support appropriate and equitable access to AI capabilities", an equity principle about access, so P51 rather than the general framework type P56 used for the sentence's other principles.
units.anchor: support appropriate and equitable access to AI capabilities
units.fit_note: States equitable access as a principle only; it says nothing about paid tools, alternatives or accommodations.

units.why: "AI should not be used to deceive, manipulate, misrepresent, circumvent established requirements or controls" is a general conduct rule against deceptive use, P74, with an academic-integrity angle ("compromise the integrity of ... teaching, or other academic work").
units.anchor: AI should not be used to deceive, manipulate, misrepresent, circumvent established requirements or controls

units.why: "individuals and units may determine that certain activities should not rely on AI" lets individuals and units opt out of AI for activities; it is a decentralised choice, P85 (units) with the individual element in a fit note.
units.anchor: individuals and units may determine that certain activities should not rely on AI
units.fit_note: Applies to individuals as well as units, and also allows alternative processes where feasible.

units.why: "Responsibility and accountability for decisions and outcomes cannot be delegated to an AI system" keeps humans responsible for decisions; P73 is closest although the sentence is general, not only about decisions on individuals.
units.anchor: Responsibility and accountability for decisions and outcomes cannot be delegated to an AI system
units.fit_note: Covers decisions and outcomes in general, not only consequential decisions about individuals.

units.why: "Users must recognize that AI systems may reflect or amplify inaccuracies, biases, or incomplete information" tells users output can be wrong or biased and to use judgment, P31.
units.anchor: AI systems may reflect or amplify inaccuracies, biases, or incomplete information

units.why: "Oversight requirements will be defined through campus AI governance processes" says where oversight rules will come from, a question of who owns the policy, P80.
units.anchor: Oversight requirements will be defined through campus AI governance processes

units.why: "should not rely on AI as a substitute for qualified professional or institutional support services" points people to human support instead of AI in sensitive personal matters, so P72 (fit is partial because it concerns wellbeing, not coursework).
units.anchor: should not rely on AI as a substitute for qualified professional or institutional support services
units.fit_note: About sensitive personal, emotional or psychological matters and wellbeing, not about course help.

units.why: Institutional decisions about AI "should, where feasible, consider resource consumption and environmental impact", a named environmental concern, P53.
units.anchor: consider resource consumption and environmental impact

units.why: The policy "governs the use of AI for University activities by all CU students, faculty, staff"; it sets the scope, P56.
units.anchor: governs the use of AI for University activities by all CU students, faculty, staff

units.why: "All use of AI for University activities must comply with applicable laws, regulations, and University policies and procedures" is a compliance duty, P77.
units.anchor: must comply with applicable laws, regulations, and University policies and procedures

units.why: "Users of AI tools must adhere to campus IT acceptable use policies" ties AI use to an existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: Users of AI tools must adhere to campus IT acceptable use policies

units.why: "Confidential and highly confidential data ... may only be entered into AI approved for the applicable data classification" limits what data can go into AI tools, P50.
units.anchor: may only be entered into AI approved for the applicable data classification

units.why: "strictly prohibited" for input of confidential data into a tool "that has not been reviewed and approved for use by campus IT"; this is a separate ban tied to tool approval but still data protection, P50.
units.anchor: input of confidential and/or highly confidential data into an AI tool that has not been

units.why: "AI tools may not be used in ways that violate conduct expectations for CU faculty, staff and students" makes the code of conduct apply to AI use, P77.
units.anchor: AI tools may not be used in ways that violate conduct expectations

units.why: "Faculty intellectual property (IP), such as course materials ... may not be submitted to AI tools for model training or other secondary uses without their express permission" protects course materials; nearest is P49, but the rule is about training and secondary use, not about students uploading.
units.anchor: may not be submitted to AI tools for model training or other secondary uses without
units.fit_note: Binds all users, concerns model training and secondary uses, and allows the faculty member's express permission.

units.why: "Students retain ownership of their original work" is a statement about ownership of student work, P52.
units.anchor: Students retain ownership of their original work

units.why: AI "prompts, outputs, and related records that are retained, must be managed in accordance with University records retention requirements"; a records-law compliance duty, P77.
units.anchor: must be managed in accordance with University records retention requirements

units.why: "The procurement of AI tools must follow the University’s procurement policies and procedures, including appropriate fiscal, cybersecurity and accessibility reviews" requires review before buying tools, P65.
units.anchor: The procurement of AI tools must follow the University’s procurement policies and procedures

units.why: "Users may not input, upload, or provide data to any AI tools if doing so would violate legal, contractual, or licensing restrictions" is a limit on data shared with AI, P50 with a fit note.
units.anchor: Users may not input, upload, or provide data to any AI tools if doing so
units.fit_note: Grounded in legal, contractual and licensing limits (HIPAA, FERPA, copyright, grants) rather than in tool vetting.

units.why: "Prompts, outputs, and related records ... may be subject to disclosure upon request" under the Colorado Open Records Act; no type covers the fact that AI prompts and outputs can become public records.
units.anchor: Prompts, outputs, and related records (including logs, where applicable) may be subject to disclosure upon
units.uncovered_note: AI prompts, outputs and logs may be public records that can be requested under the Colorado Open Records Act.

units.why: Units and individuals deploying AI "are responsible ... for complying with applicable laws, regulations, and University policies", a compliance duty on those who deploy tools, P77.
units.anchor: are responsible, within the scope of their roles and authority, for complying with applicable laws

units.why: "AI-derived content used for official communications must comply with branding, communication, marketing, photography, videography, and web policies" governs AI in official communications, P76.
units.anchor: AI-derived content used for official communications must comply with branding, communication, marketing

units.why: "University data ... must not be used for external or commercial AI model training unless explicitly authorized" limits sharing of university data with AI providers, P65.
units.anchor: must not be used for external or commercial AI model training unless explicitly authorized

units.why: "The University will maintain and communicate guidance on approved AI tools" commits the university to publish an approved-tool list, P92.
units.anchor: The University will maintain and communicate guidance on approved AI tools

units.why: "The University shall establish a structure of advisory committees" names the bodies that inform AI decisions, P80.
units.anchor: The University shall establish a structure of advisory committees

units.why: "Each campus Chancellor (or designee) shall appoint a Campus AI committee(s) to implement this Policy on their campus and develop further campus-specific policy" names the campus owner of the policy, P80.
units.anchor: shall appoint a Campus AI committee(s) to implement this Policy on their campus

units.why: Faculty shared governance bodies "are responsible for establishing and maintaining faculty-led committees or processes" for instructional AI use; who owns academic AI guidance, P80.
units.anchor: responsible for establishing and maintaining faculty-led committees or processes

units.why: "individual faculty shall ensure that AI use aligns with academic standards, disciplinary norms, institutional practices, and pedagogical goals" ties faculty AI decisions to pedagogical goals; P83 (fit partial).
units.anchor: individual faculty shall ensure that AI use aligns with academic standards, disciplinary norms
units.fit_note: Also names academic standards, disciplinary norms and institutional practices, not only learning objectives.

units.why: "The President shall appoint a Systemwide AI Committee to support coordination and oversight" names the system-level body, P80.
units.anchor: The President shall appoint a Systemwide AI Committee to support coordination and oversight

units.why: "Before implementing or deploying any new AI tool ... review and approval processes are followed" requires approval before deployment, P65.
units.anchor: Before implementing or deploying any new AI tool for University Activities

units.why: The review "may include evaluation of" privacy, security, accessibility, legal and bias risks; this lists review criteria for tools, P65.
units.anchor: may include evaluation of

units.why: "Users must disclose their use of GenAI to an appropriate audience when such use contributes to University decisions or other high‑impact outputs" is a disclosure duty, P24, but limited to official high-impact outputs and not coursework.
units.anchor: Users must disclose their use of GenAI to an appropriate audience
units.fit_note: Applies only to high-impact outputs in an official University capacity, not to student coursework.

units.why: "individuals using GenAI are responsible for reviewing outputs for accuracy, appropriateness" makes users check output before relying on it, P31.
units.anchor: individuals using GenAI are responsible for reviewing outputs for accuracy, appropriateness

units.why: "this policy does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework" leaves the coursework decision to others, P04; no default stance is set.
units.anchor: this policy does not dictate the use or non-use of AI tools in coursework
units.fit_note: Cites academic freedom and gives the decision to schools, colleges, departments or programs (next sentence) as well as instructors.

units.why: "Schools, colleges, departments, or academic programs ... may establish guidance regarding the use of GenAI in coursework" lets units set their own rules, P85.
units.anchor: may establish guidance regarding the use of GenAI in coursework or instructional activities

units.why: "Such guidance must be consistent with this APS and applicable campus policies and procedures" limits unit guidance to fit university policy, P77.
units.anchor: Such guidance must be consistent with this APS and applicable campus policies and procedures

units.why: "Faculty shared governance bodies and professional academic organizations can develop best practices" for GenAI in research, so P62.
units.anchor: can develop best practices for risk management strategies regarding the use of GenAI tools in

units.why: "University staff may use GenAI tools to support administrative, operational, and service functions" permits staff use, P76.
units.anchor: University staff may use GenAI tools to support administrative, operational, and service functions

units.why: "Supervisors and units may establish additional guidance for the appropriate use of GenAI in administrative functions" lets units add rules for administrative AI use, P76.
units.anchor: Supervisors and units may establish additional guidance for the appropriate use of GenAI

units.why: GenAI depictions of real people "must not be created or distributed without their explicit, informed consent"; a ban on deceptive or harmful synthetic media, P74.
units.anchor: must not be created or distributed without their explicit, informed consent

units.why: "GenAI tools may not be used to intentionally create sexualized content" depicting real individuals is a conduct ban on harmful AI use, P74.
units.anchor: GenAI tools may not be used to intentionally create sexualized content

units.why: Users "must perform due diligence to ensure that outputs do not infringe copyright", a copyright duty for AI output, P52.
units.anchor: must perform due diligence to ensure that outputs do not infringe copyright

units.why: "Policy violations may result in disciplinary action ... student conduct processes" sends violations into existing conduct processes, P36.
units.anchor: Policy violations may result in disciplinary action consistent with applicable University policies and procedures
units.fit_note: Covers violations of the whole AI policy (employee discipline, loss of access, legal remedies), not only academic misconduct.

units.why: "This Policy will be reviewed on a periodic basis and more frequently as needed" sets a review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: This Policy will be reviewed on a periodic basis and more frequently as needed

units.why: The "AI tool" definition ("a commercial or non-commercial technology that includes artificial intelligence-based capabilities", including embedded AI such as "a word processor with AI-based content feedback") sets scope, P61.
units.anchor: technology that includes artificial intelligence-based capabilities

documents.unit: Boulder Faculty Assembly and Center for Teaching & Learning
documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Syllabus Guidance
documents.summary: A draft (12/23/24) from the Boulder Faculty Assembly and Center for Teaching and Learning that gives instructors four levels of AI use and sample syllabus language. It also advises on discussing rules with students, avoiding detectors, and citing AI use.
documents.stance_why: The guidance offers four levels ("Full Gen AI Use", "No Gen AI Use", "Conditional Gen AI Use", "Limited Gen AI Use") and says "Whether you choose to prohibit, allow, or conditionally permit gen AI usage", so it offers tiers and leaves the choice to instructors.

units.why: The note says this is "a living document that will be amended in response to significant developments", a statement that the guidance will change, P54.
units.anchor: a living document that will be amended in response to significant developments

units.why: "Let these four levels of use kick off the conversation" names four levels (Full, No, Conditional, Limited), which is P05.
units.anchor: Let these four levels of use kick off the conversation

units.why: "educators should communicate to students their policies regarding the use of these tools in coursework" asks every instructor to state a policy, P09.
units.anchor: educators should communicate to students their policies regarding the use of these tools in coursework

units.why: "a number of gen AI considerations to take into account including ethical, privacy, security, environmental, financial, and accessibility concerns" lists concerns for instructors; nearest P53 (partial).
units.anchor: ethical, privacy, security, environmental, financial, and accessibility concerns
units.fit_note: Also names privacy, security, financial and accessibility concerns, which other types cover separately.

units.why: "Whether you choose to prohibit, allow, or conditionally permit gen AI usage" leaves the choice to the instructor, P04; the clearer statement is to "prevent misunderstandings".
units.anchor: Whether you choose to prohibit, allow, or conditionally permit gen AI usage

units.why: "A thoughtful conversation with students addressing your expectations ... can encourage open dialogue and promote trust" asks instructors to discuss the rules with students, P66.
units.anchor: A thoughtful conversation with students addressing your expectations about gen AI use

units.why: "Consider co-designing a gen AI use policy with your students collaboratively" is the co-creation type, P67.
units.anchor: Consider co-designing a gen AI use policy with your students collaboratively

units.why: "Turnitin AI Writing Detector or other gen AI detector tools are unreliable and not recommended" says detectors should not be relied on, P39.
units.anchor: detector tools are unreliable and not recommended

units.why: "If you plan to use any gen AI detection, you should disclose this in your syllabus" is an instructor disclosure of their own tool use, P47 (partial, since it is detection rather than AI generation).
units.anchor: If you plan to use any gen AI detection, you should disclose this in your
units.fit_note: The disclosed instructor practice is AI detection of student work, not instructor use of generative AI.

units.why: "consider whether students can meaningfully consent to use of such tools to assess their work" raises student consent to detectors; no type covers consent to AI-based assessment of student work.
units.anchor: whether students can meaningfully consent to use of such tools to assess their work
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should consider whether students can meaningfully consent to AI detection tools being used to assess their work.

units.why: "The guidance below is intended for instructors to use on their syllabus statements, or as a starting point" states how the guidance is to be used; this is the purpose of the framework, P56.
units.anchor: intended for instructors to use on their syllabus statements, or as a starting point

units.why: "developed using the Pepperdine Generative AI Syllabus statement Tool and adapted for use at CU Boulder" says how the statements were made, P84.
units.anchor: developed using the Pepperdine Generative AI Syllabus statement Tool

units.why: "This statement governs all such tools, including those released during our semester together" sets the sample statement's scope across all current and future tools, P61.
units.anchor: This statement governs all such tools, including those released during our semester together

units.why: "the goal of gen AI tools is to reproduce content that seems to have been produced by a human, not to produce accurate or reliable content" warns outputs may be wrong, P31.
units.anchor: not to produce accurate or reliable content

units.why: "It is your responsibility—not the tool’s—to assure the quality, integrity, and accuracy of work you submit" makes students accountable for submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: It is your responsibility—not the tool’s—to assure the quality, integrity, and accuracy of work

units.why: "If gen AI tool use is suspected ... in ways not explicitly authorized, I will follow up with you" has the instructor speak with the student first, P57.
units.anchor: I will follow up with you

units.why: "I may contact the Office of Student Conduct & Conflict Resolution to report suspected Honor Code violations" treats unauthorized AI as an Honor Code matter handled by the conduct office, P36.
units.anchor: contact the Office of Student Conduct & Conflict Resolution to report suspected Honor Code violations

units.why: "you must be wary of unintentional plagiarism or data fabrication" warns that AI use can create plagiarism or fabricated data, nearest P31 (partial).
units.anchor: you must be wary of unintentional plagiarism or data fabrication
units.fit_note: Warns of unintentional plagiarism and data fabrication, a risk that comes with AI output, not only inaccuracy.

units.why: "it is recommended that you incorporate one of the following four categories ... so that students clearly understand your expectations" asks instructors to use the tiers, P05.
units.anchor: incorporate one of the following four categories about generative AI tool use in your classroom

units.why: "You may also consider using these categories to specify allowable use for individual assignments" lets the level be set per assignment, P04.
units.anchor: using these categories to specify allowable use for individual assignments

units.why: Full Gen AI Use: "You may use gen AI tools in this course however you see fit" is a permissive default, P02.
units.anchor: You may use gen AI tools in this course however you see fit

units.why: "some assignments will require the use of such tools" says AI use is required in some work, P79.
units.anchor: some assignments will require the use of such tools

units.why: "keep in mind your own and others' privacy implications and security risks when using gen AI tools" is a privacy caution, P50.
units.anchor: keep in mind your own and others' privacy implications and security risks

units.why: "document your usage with the Chicago Manual of Style or appropriate citation guidelines for this course" requires citing AI use; the same sentence is repeated in the Conditional and Limited statements and the TIP and is coded once, P24.
units.anchor: document your usage with the Chicago Manual of Style or appropriate citation guidelines for this

units.why: "consider providing alternative methods that do not require gen AI use to complete the assignment" is an equity and access rule for instructors, P51.
units.anchor: consider providing alternative methods that do not require gen AI use to complete the assignment

units.why: No Gen AI Use: "You may not use gen AI tools on any assignments in this course" is a ban on all assignments, P01.
units.anchor: You may not use gen AI tools on any assignments in this course

units.why: "consider including clarifying language as to why" asks instructors who ban AI to give their reasons, P66.
units.anchor: clarifying language as to why

units.why: "to outline consequences of gen AI use" asks instructors to state consequences in the syllabus; the sample gives a redo, so P37 (partial because it is advice to state consequences).
units.anchor: outline consequences of gen AI use
units.fit_note: Advises instructors to state consequences; no concrete penalty is set here.

units.why: The sample says "Gen AI use in this course will not enhance student learning, nor serve the topic at hand", the reason for a ban, P41 (partial).
units.anchor: Gen AI use in this course will not enhance student learning, nor serve the topic
units.fit_note: Says AI will not enhance learning but does not say that doing the work yourself builds skill.

units.why: "I will consult with you and ask that you redo the assignment using no gen AI within X number of days" offers a redo rather than only a penalty, P68.
units.anchor: ask that you redo the assignment using no gen AI

units.why: "clarify whether use of tools such as Grammarly and Spellcheckers is acceptable or unacceptable" asks instructors to decide on prose tools, P18.
units.anchor: clarify whether use of tools such as Grammarly and Spellcheckers is acceptable or unacceptable
units.fit_note: Leaves the decision open for writing tools; it does not itself permit or ban them.

units.why: Conditional Gen AI Use: "You may conditionally use gen AI tools in this course on any assignment" allows AI on all assignments under conditions, P02.
units.anchor: You may conditionally use gen AI tools in this course on any assignment
units.fit_note: Permission is conditional on the instructor's listed conditions rather than open.

units.why: "with clear attribution and explanation of AI's role in the completion of the assignment" requires students to say how AI contributed, P24.
units.anchor: with clear attribution and explanation of AI's role in the completion of the assignment
units.fit_note: Asks for attribution plus an explanation of AI's role, beyond a citation.

units.why: Limited Gen AI Use: "their use is limited to the following particular tasks" allows AI on specific assignments only for listed tasks, a narrow permission, P04 (the instructor lists the tasks).
units.anchor: their use is limited to the following particular tasks
units.fit_note: Permits AI only for tasks the instructor lists, per assignment.

units.why: The example "grammar checks but not for rewriting sections of the assignment" permits grammar checking only, P91.
units.anchor: grammar checks but not for rewriting sections of the assignment
units.fit_note: Allows grammar checks but not rewriting.

units.why: The example "generating ideas or outlines, but the final work must be student-generated" allows idea generation with student-authored final work, P15.
units.anchor: generating ideas or outlines, but the final work must be student-generated
units.fit_note: Also requires the final work to be student-generated.

units.why: The example "summarizing or synthesizing research, with proper critical evaluation and original analysis" permits AI summaries if the student evaluates critically, P14.
units.anchor: summarizing or synthesizing research, with proper critical evaluation and original analysis
units.fit_note: Summaries of research are allowed only with the student's critical evaluation and original analysis.

units.why: "you may have some assignments for which you require gen AI use for specific pedagogical purposes" tells instructors they can require AI, P79.
units.anchor: you may have some assignments for which you require gen AI use

units.why: "clearly describe how gen AI use meets the learning goals of the assignment" ties required AI use to learning goals, P83.
units.anchor: clearly describe how gen AI use meets the learning goals of the assignment

units.why: "take into consideration accessibility parameters" asks instructors who require AI to consider accessibility, P97.
units.anchor: take into consideration accessibility parameters

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Security Guidelines
documents.summary: A CU Boulder Office of Information Technology page of data-security guidelines for generative AI. It limits AI tool use to Public data, points to campus-recommended tools, and asks users to verify output and vendor terms. It says nothing about coursework.
documents.stance_why: The page gives data-security rules ("AI tool use is only approved for data classified as Public") and does not say whether AI may be used in teaching or coursework, so it sets no academic stance; nearest enum value is delegates.

units.why: "Implementation of AI is subject to all applicable CU Boulder policies, standards and guidelines" ties AI use to existing campus policy, P77.
units.anchor: Implementation of AI is subject to all applicable CU Boulder policies, standards and guidelines

units.why: "This page is intended to guide our community as you consider using AI on the CU Boulder campus" states the page's purpose and scope (data security), P56.
units.anchor: This page is intended to guide our community as you consider using AI on the

units.why: "Use AI tools available and recommended for use on the CU Boulder campus" tells users to prefer campus-vetted tools, P92.
units.anchor: Use AI tools available and recommended for use on the CU Boulder campus

units.why: "AI tool use is only approved for data classified as Public" limits what data may be used with AI tools, P50.
units.anchor: AI tool use is only approved for data classified as Public

units.why: Sharing Confidential data with an AI service means "the service needs to be reviewed for compliance with CU’s data security requirements via ICT Review", a tool review requirement, P65.
units.anchor: the service needs to be reviewed for compliance with CU’s data security requirements

units.why: "Information shared with Generative AI tools using default settings is not private" warns that prompts are exposed, P50.
units.anchor: Information shared with Generative AI tools using default settings is not private

units.why: "Review AI tool output to verify integrity: the output should be accurate and not incomplete, incorrect, or biased" asks users to verify output, P31.
units.anchor: Review AI tool output to verify integrity

units.why: "AI-generated computer code should NOT be used for institutional IT systems and services unless it has been reviewed by a human" allows AI code only under a review condition, nearest P16, though it concerns institutional IT systems and not coursework.
units.anchor: AI-generated computer code should NOT be used for institutional IT systems and services unless it
units.fit_note: Concerns code for institutional IT systems, not student work; the condition is human review for accuracy, security and efficiency.

units.why: "must read and understand the AI tool vendor’s policies" makes faculty, staff and students check the vendor's terms of use, P52.
units.anchor: must read and understand the AI tool vendor’s policies
units.fit_note: Concerns vendor terms of use and data handling more than copyright or ownership.

units.why: "A great framework to help you determine whether an AI tool is reliable and/or truthful is the NIST AI Risk Management framework" recommends a framework for judging AI output, nearest P31.
units.anchor: A great framework to help you determine whether an AI tool is reliable and/or truthful
units.fit_note: Recommends a risk framework to judge tool reliability, not a rule to verify each output.

units.why: "standards and expectations for bias minimization should be defined prior to using AI" names bias as a concern, P53.
units.anchor: standards and expectations for bias minimization should be defined prior to using AI

units.why: "understanding when one is working with AI-generated (rather than human-generated) information" describes transparency as knowing when AI is involved, nearest P103.
units.anchor: understanding when one is working with AI-generated (rather than human-generated) information
units.fit_note: A definition of transparency within the NIST framework summary, not a duty to tell people.

notes: Course layer was deferred; no school or computing documents found by the collector. The syllabus guidance PDF text is one word per line, so anchors were matched with whitespace folding. The same Chicago-style citation sentence appears three times in the syllabus guidance and is coded once. The OIT page stance is set to delegates because the enum has no value for a document with no coursework stance.
